ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *h₂er-der. Proto-Italic *ordōder. Latin ōrdinem Old French ordneder. Middle English ordre English order From Middle English ordre, from Old French ordre, ordne, ordene (“order, rank”), from Latin ōrdinem, accusative of ōrdō (“row, rank, regular arrangement”, literally “row of threads in a loom”), from Proto-Italic *ordō (“to arrange”), probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂or-d-, from *h₂er-. Related to Latin ōrdior (“begin”, literally “begin to weave”). In sense “request for purchase”, compare bespoke. Doublet of ordo.

senses.d: Arrangement, disposition, or sequence.
ex: put the children in age order
It's arranged in order of frequency

senses.d: A position in an arrangement, disposition, or sequence.
ex: This narrative must be discussed later on, in its order.
The latter comes into play only as we examine each word in its order in the line.

senses.d: The state of being well arranged.
ex: The house is in order; the machinery is out of order.

senses.d: Conformity with law or decorum; freedom from disturbance; general tranquillity; public quiet.
ex: to preserve order in a community or an assembly
Order in the court!

senses.d: A command.
ex: give an order
his inability to follow orders

senses.d: A request for some product or service; a commission to purchase, sell, or supply goods.
ex: make an order
place an online order for the new range of sunglasses

senses.d: The goods requested.
ex: Your order should arrive within two days.
The waiter brought our orders to the table, but forgot the cutlery.

senses.d: A group of religious adherents, especially monks or nuns, set apart within their religion by adherence to a particular rule or set of principles.
ex: St. Ignatius Loyola founded the Jesuit order in 1537.

senses.d: An association of knights.
ex: the Order of the Garter, the Order of the Bath.

senses.d: Any group of people with common interests.
To set in some sort of order.
ex: We need to order them alphabetically.

senses.d: To arrange, set in proper order.
ex: The books in the shelf need ordering.

senses.d: To issue a command to; to charge.
ex: to order troops to advance
He ordered me to leave.

senses.d: To request some product or service; to secure by placing an order.
ex: You can now order most products to be delivered to your home.
to order groceries

senses.d: To admit to holy orders; to ordain; to receive into the ranks of the ministry.
ex: persons presented to be ordered deacons

senses.d: A person having immediate jurisdiction in a given case of ecclesiastical law, such as the bishop within a diocese.
A courier; someone delivering mail or post.
ex: I […] will lay to till you come within hail […] but pray respond by the first ordinary.

senses.d: A judge with the authority to deal with cases himself or herself rather than by delegation.
The chaplain of Newgate prison, who prepared condemned prisoners for death.
ex: He died with pious composure and resolution. I have just seen the Ordinary that attended him.

senses.d: Customary fare, one's regular daily allowance of food; (hence) a regular portion or allowance.

ex: Here he recommended me to fix my board, there being an excellent ordinary daily at two o'clock, at which I might dine or not as I pleased.

senses.d: A place where such meals are served; a public tavern, inn.

senses.d: One of the standard geometric designs placed across the center of a coat of arms, such as a pale or fess.

senses.d: The usual course of things; normal condition or health; a standard way of behaviour or action.
ex: I ſee no more in you than in the ordinary / Of nature's ſalework.

senses.d: Having regular jurisdiction; now only used in certain phrases.
Being part of the natural order of things; normal, customary, routine.
ex: On an ordinary day I wake up at nine o'clock, work for six hours, and then go to the gym.

senses.d: Having no special characteristics or function; everyday, common, mundane; often deprecatory.
ex: I live a very ordinary life most of the time, but every year I spend a week in Antarctica.

senses.d: Bad or undesirable.
